items.summaryEn: Broadcaster Naomi Schiff has warned that Red Bull's narrow set-up window could compromise Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar's 2026 Formula 1 campaigns.
detailZh: 娜奥米·希夫警告红牛赛车调校窗口过窄
娜奥米·希夫对红牛赛车狭窄的工作窗口表达了担忧
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术解析与比赛分析。
评论员娜奥米·希夫警告，红牛赛车调校窗口过窄，可能影响马克斯·维斯塔潘和伊萨克·哈贾尔2026赛季的一级方程式征程。
在美国大奖赛上，两位车手的比赛在开局阶段都遭遇了挫折。哈贾尔遇到了起步问题，这促使他要求重新设计离合器；而维斯塔潘在1号弯出弯时缺乏电力部署，这立刻让他陷入了与法拉利车队贯穿全场的缠斗。
在Up To Speed播客节目中，希夫认为比赛起步时的问题反映了米尔顿凯恩斯车队更广泛的问题。
希夫说：“很遗憾他们俩都没能顺利起步，因为我们本来很期待马克斯和基米之间的较量，而且伊萨克也在其中，这本来真的可能制造一点冷门，谁知道呢，说不定还能拿下他在一级方程式的首场胜利。”
“但整个周末那辆红牛，感觉除了离合器之外，还有很多地方需要审视。感觉那辆车真正有效的工作窗口并不大，而且真的处在刀刃边缘，这几年来一直如此。”
“我想，从今天一开始，对他们来说这更像是一场止损的比赛。而马克斯在最后也承认，也许他们从一开始制定的策略就不对。”
“我们也听到他在无线电里情绪相当激动，抱怨车队把他放回脏空气里，也许没有优化他们最终不得不采用的策略。但目前那辆车对那两位车手来说似乎都不太好驾驶。”
detailEn: Naomi Schiff warns Red Bull over "knife's edge" F1 car after US GP struggles
Naomi Schiff has raised concerns over Red Bull's narrow operating window
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.
Broadcaster Naomi Schiff has warned that Red Bull's narrow set-up window could be compromising Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar's 2026 Formula 1 campaigns.

At the United States Grand Prix, both drivers' races were derailed in the opening stages. Hadjar suffered a launch issue that prompted him to demand a clutch redesign, while Verstappen lacked electrical deployment out of Turn 1, which instantly dropped him into a race-long battle with the Ferraris.
Speaking on the Up To Speed podcast, Schiff argued that the problems at the start of the race are indicative of wider issues for the Milton Keynes outfit.

"It was such a shame that they both didn't get off the line there because it was a battle we were looking forward to between Max and Kimi, but then also Isack being in there could have really caused a little bit of an upset and potentially, who knows, clinched his first victory in Formula 1," Schiff said.

"But that Red Bull this whole weekend, it just feels like there's, besides the clutch, there's a lot that needs to be looked at. It feels like there's really not a very big operational window that works with that car, and that it's really on a knife's edge, as it has been for a number of years now.
"I guess it was more of a damage limitation race for them from the get-go today. And Max admitting at the end that maybe the strategy call that they had from the beginning wasn't right.

"We heard him over the radio being pretty passionate as well about them sending him back out into dirty air and maybe not optimising the strategy that they ended up having to go with. But that car just doesn't seem to be very easy to drive for either of those drivers at the moment."

items.originalTitle: Fred Vasseur reveals two costly moments that denied Ferrari US GP double podium
detailZh: 弗雷德·瓦瑟尔透露两起代价高昂的时刻，导致法拉利美国大奖赛错失双料领奖台
弗雷德·瓦瑟尔解释了Q3灾难和由凯迪拉克引发的晚些时候的VSC如何让法拉利失去了这个机会
对于法拉利车迷来说，这是最新的Scuderia 法拉利 F1新闻，包括车手更新、技术分析和来自马拉内洛及更远处的赛事反应
如果严格根据成绩单来看，美国大奖赛对法拉利来说是一个极为成功的周末。新升级的赛车拥有惊人的比赛速度，轮胎磨损完全在控制之中，查尔斯·勒克莱尔驾驶着他的赛车在梅赛德斯-奔驰的基米·安东内利之后取得了精彩的第二名
但是，在Scuderia车队的维修区里，有一种挥之不去的'如果'的感觉
如果这个周末在美洲赛车场的比赛中，只有两件事略有不同，法拉利老板弗雷德·瓦瑟尔坚信他们将会获得巨大的双料领奖台——甚至可能获得比赛的胜利
在他的赛后采访中，天空体育F1的记者特德·克拉维茨向瓦瑟尔建议，查尔斯·勒克莱尔实际上在不同的情况下有赢得比赛的潜在速度。不出所料，瓦瑟尔完全同意，将团队周六的表现视为周日问题根源
'可能吧，我认为今天一切都很顺利，一切都很好，速度也不错，我们在策略上很积极，因为我们必须超越对手，'瓦瑟尔解释说。'总的来说，如果我们错过了什么，那可能就是昨天Q3的最后两圈；我认为这可能是周末最重要的一圈，也是我们出现问题的地方。
因为在现代一级方程式赛车中，赛道位置绝对是王道，错过关键的Q3窗口意味着法拉利不得不在车流中烧胎挣扎，而安东内利则在前面享受着干净的空气。
尽管错过了胜利，法拉利在比赛的最后阶段积极追赶红牛的马克斯·维斯塔潘。刘易斯·汉密尔顿以惊人的速度追击着挣扎的小红牛22，为最后的领奖台位置准备了一场精彩的对决。
然后，最讽刺的事情发生了。
瓦尔特里·博塔斯遭遇机械故障，将他的凯迪拉克开到赛道边，引发了一场晚期的虚拟安全车，这完全中和了比赛，并保住了维斯塔潘的第三名奖杯。
Kravitz 幽默地指出法拉利的亮点：博塔斯的凯迪拉克使用的是法拉利动力单元，但由于汽车无法移动，显然是液压故障——这意味着不是法拉利部件爆炸。
尽管瓦瑟尔可能庆幸他的客户引擎没有爆炸，但VSC介入的时间对汉密尔顿来说却是毁灭性的。
瓦瑟尔承认，如果没有VSC，可能本可以拿到双料领奖台。他遗憾地表示，'他正在逼近，然后我不知道是第三还是第四名；我没有水晶球，但最终速度是有的。'
尽管错过了双料领奖台，瓦瑟尔离开德克萨斯州时对车队带到COTA的备受瞩目的空气动力学升级套件感到非常乐观。
“是的，一切还可以，但下周我们一定要做得更好，”瓦瑟尔总结道，完美地掩饰了巨大的速度提升。'“我们必须调整好一切，并再次回到这个状态，但让我们继续努力。”
“如果法拉利能清理掉他们的Q3执行问题，并避免更多不及时的凯迪拉克故障，他们将在下周周末的高海拔墨西哥大奖赛上成为绝对的威胁。”
detailEn: Fred Vasseur reveals two costly moments that denied Ferrari US GP double podium
Fred Vasseur explains how a Q3 disaster and a late VSC triggered by a Cadillac cost Ferrari a massive double podium
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.

The United States Grand Prix was a wildly successful weekend for Ferrari, if you strictly go off the timing sheets. The newly upgraded car possessed blazing-fast race pace, tyre degradation was fully under control, and Charles Leclerc dragged his machine to a brilliant second-place finish behind Mercedes’ Kimi Antonelli.
But inside the Scuderia garage, there is a lingering feeling of "what if."

If just two things had gone slightly differently this weekend at the Circuit of the Americas, Ferrari boss Fred Vasseur is convinced they would have secured a massive double podium—and potentially even the outright race victory.

During his post-race interview with Sky Sports F1, reporter Ted Kravitz suggested to Vasseur that Charles Leclerc actually had the underlying pace to win the race under different circumstances. Unsurprisingly, Vasseur completely agreed, pointing the finger at the team's Saturday performance as the root of their Sunday problems.

"Probably yes, I think that today it went well, everything went well, the pace was OK, we were aggressive with the strategy, because we had to overtake," Vasseur explained. "Overall, if we missed something, it's the last two laps in Q3 yesterday; I think it was the most important lap of the weekend probably, and it's where we had the issue."

Because track position is absolutely king in modern Formula 1, missing that critical Q3 window meant Ferrari had to burn their tyres fighting through traffic while Antonelli cruised in clean air at the front.

Despite missing the win, Ferrari was actively hunting down Red Bull's Max Verstappen in the closing stages of the race. Lewis Hamilton was reeling in the struggling RB22 at a rapid pace, setting up a blockbuster battle for the final podium spot.
And then, the ultimate irony struck.

Valtteri Bottas suffered a mechanical failure and pulled his Cadillac over to the side of the track, triggering a late virtual safety car that completely neutralised the race and saved Verstappen's third-place trophy.

Kravitz hilariously pointed out the silver lining for Ferrari: Bottas' Cadillac uses a Ferrari power unit, but because the car couldn't be moved, it was clearly a hydraulic failure—which means it wasn't a Ferrari part that exploded.
While Vasseur was likely relieved his customer engine didn't blow up, the timing of the VSC was devastating for Hamilton.

"Without the VSC, probably it would have been a double podium," Vasseur admitted, lamenting the lost opportunity. "He was closing, and then I don't know if it was P3 or P4; I don't have the crystal ball, but at the end of the day the pace was there."
Despite missing out on the double podium, Vasseur is leaving Texas feeling highly optimistic about the heavily scrutinised aero upgrade package the team brought to COTA.

"Yes, everything was OK-ish, but now for sure we have to do a better job next week," Vasseur concluded, perfectly downplaying the massive pace injection. "We have to fine-tune everything and to come back on this, but let's continue to push."
If Ferrari can clean up their Q3 execution and avoid any more poorly timed Cadillac breakdowns, they are going to be an absolute menace at the high-altitude Mexican Grand Prix next weekend.

items.originalTitle: Red Bull reveals damage behind Max Verstappen's US GP struggles
items.summaryEn: Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies said debris on lap 8 caused Max Verstappen's pace drop at the United States Grand Prix, and promised to fix Isack Hadjar's clutch issues.
detailZh: 红牛披露维斯塔潘美国大奖赛速度下滑背后的损伤
洛朗·梅基斯将维斯塔潘的速度下滑归咎于第8圈的碎片，同时承诺解决伊萨克·哈贾尔的离合器问题
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术洞察与比赛分析。
当你的明星车手拿下领奖台后走下赛车，随即在全球直播中直言维修区停站、轮胎和发动机制动全都糟糕透顶时，车队领队就得赶紧拿起最近的麦克风去灭火。
在美国大奖赛上维斯塔潘通过无线电大发雷霆之后，红牛车队首席执行官兼领队洛朗·梅基斯全面进入了公关危机管控模式。梅基斯没有把调校失误的责任推给工程部门，而是把矛头指向了某块不听话的碳纤维。
当马克斯·维斯塔潘抱怨选错了轮胎配方、还要应付糟糕的发动机制动时，梅基斯却声称，赛车在起步灯熄灭后仅仅几分钟就受了伤。
“马克斯的赛车在第8圈左右撞到了一些碎片，因此受了些损伤，”梅基斯在赛后接受媒体采访时表示。“除此之外，我们还有几个问题影响了平衡，结果就是速度掉了、轮胎衰退加剧，马克斯没能守住第二名。”
梅基斯承认，车队根本没有足够的火力去追赶分站冠军基米·安东内利，后者相对轻松地一路驶向得克萨斯的夕阳。
“可以这么说，尽管马克斯以第三名完赛、拿下本赛季第12个领奖台，我们离开奥斯汀时并不完全满意，”车队领队坦言。“今天我们失去了一些优势，我认为我们的速度不足以与基米抗衡，他跑了一场非常强劲的比赛，所以要向他表示祝贺。”
维斯塔潘并不是周日唯一在头盔里大喊的车手。他的队友伊萨克·哈贾尔因离合器故障遭遇了灾难性的起步，随后无线电完全失联，毁掉了他的进站策略。梅基斯没有回避这些机械故障，直接承认车队严重辜负了这位年轻车手。
“伊萨克的情况类似，他的比赛被起步以及比赛中的几个问题所拖累，”梅基斯承认。“起步再次不够完美，但车队正在努力确保我们拥有在未来解决这一问题的工具。”
红牛在 championship 中的一线希望
尽管两位车手都极其讨厌他们的赛车在美洲赛道上的操控表现，红牛实际上却带着一个绝佳的积分榜位置离开了这个比赛周末。
“这是一个充满挑战的周日，但我们会接受这个领奖台，因为我们知道今天没有完全发挥出赛车的潜力，我们会从本周末吸取经验，下周在墨西哥以更强的姿态回归，”梅基斯指出，随后强调了这一巨大的利好。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，伊萨克·哈贾尔，红牛车队
“尽管如此，我们现在已经升至车队积分榜第三位，而马克斯在车手积分榜上距离第二名也仅差六分。”
如果红牛能找到办法阻止小红牛22过度消耗自身离合器，同时针对墨西哥城高海拔空气调校好空气动力学平衡，那么维斯塔潘就处于有利位置，有望在赛季结束前锁定积分榜第二名。
detailEn: Red Bull reveals damage behind Max Verstappen's US GP struggles
Laurent Mekies blames lap 8 debris for Max Verstappen's pace drop while promising to fix Isack Hadjar's clutch issues
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

When your star driver gets out of the car after grabbing a podium and immediately tells the global broadcast that the pitstops, tyres, and engine braking were all complete garbage, it is up to the team principal to jump on the nearest microphone and put out the fire.

Following Verstappen's radio meltdown at the United States Grand Prix, Red Bull Racing CEO and team principal Laurent Mekies went into full PR damage control mode. Instead of blaming the engineering department for botching the set-up, Mekies pointed the finger at some rogue carbon fibre.
While Max Verstappen complained about picking the wrong tyre compounds and dealing with awful engine braking, Mekies claimed the car was actually wounded just a few minutes after the lights went out.

"Max’s car hit some debris around lap eight and picked up some damage," Mekies stated while speaking with the media after the race. "On top of that, we had a few issues that hurt the balance and, as a result, the pace dropped off, the degradation increased, and Max couldn't hang on to second place."
Mekies admitted the team simply didn't have the firepower to chase down race-winner Kimi Antonelli, who drove off into the Texas sunset relatively unchallenged.

"It’s fair to say that, despite a 12th podium of the season with Max finishing third, we are leaving Austin not fully satisfied," the team principal confessed. "We lost a bit of our edge today, and I don't think we had enough pace to fight with Kimi, who had a very strong race, so well done to him."

Verstappen wasn't the only driver screaming into his helmet on Sunday. His team-mate Isack Hadjar suffered a catastrophic start due to a faulty clutch, followed by a total radio blackout that ruined his pit strategy. Mekies didn't shy away from the mechanical failures, directly acknowledging that the team severely let the young driver down.

"It was a similar story for Isack, whose race was compromised by the start and then by a couple of problems during the race," Mekies admitted. "Once again, the starts weren’t perfect, but the team is working to make sure we have the tools to fix that in the future."
The championship silver lining for Red Bull
Despite both drivers absolutely hating how their cars handled at the Circuit of the Americas, Red Bull actually walked away from the weekend in a fantastic mathematical position.

"A challenging Sunday, but we’ll take the podium knowing that we didn’t fully realise the potential of the car today, and we’ll take learnings from this weekend to come back stronger next week in Mexico," Mekies noted before highlighting the massive silver lining.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing
"Despite all that, we have now moved up to third in the constructors’ championship, and Max is now only six points behind second place in the drivers’ championship.”

If Red Bull can figure out how to stop the RB22 from eating its own clutch while dialling in the aerodynamic balance for the high-altitude air in Mexico City, Verstappen is in prime position to claim P2 in the standings before the season ends.

items.summaryZh: 前F1车手大卫·库尔特哈德否认了车手可以将糟糕表现归咎于2026年新赛规的说法，强调历史上伟大的车手都能适应任何赛车。

media.altZh: 库尔特哈德否认将F1新规作为表现不佳的借口 · 第 1 张

items.originalTitle: David Coulthard rejects F1 regulation excuses with Ayrton Senna and Michael Schumacher comparison
detailZh: 大卫·库尔特哈德拒绝用阿yrton Senna和迈克尔·舒马赫的比较来为F1规则辩解
大卫·库尔特哈德否认了2026年F1规则是导致车手们陷入困境的原因的说法
大卫·库尔特哈德在冲刺赛的起跑线上
赛车文化超越赛道。车手的生活方式、时尚、旅行、设计和那些让赛车不仅仅是一项运动的故事。
前一级方程式车手大卫·库尔特哈德驳斥了车手可以将糟糕的表现归咎于锦标赛新2026年规定的说法，坚称所有时间最伟大的车手都能成功适应任何机械。
F1在2026年引入了一项重大规则变更。虽然一些车手在从新一代赛车中提取一致速度方面遇到了困难，但库尔特哈德认为，车手的基准表现不应受到规则手册的影响。
在美国大奖赛之后，这位13次大奖赛冠军在《Up To Speed》播客中提到了自己的职业生涯，以驳斥某些赛车不适合某些车手的观点。
“我开过主动赛车、被动赛车、3.5升、3升、2.4升、沟槽轮胎、光头胎、轮胎战，坦白说，我在所有这些赛车上的表现相对相同，我在排位赛中缺少了十分之一秒，这使得你在赛道位置上难以与队友竞争，”库尔特哈德解释道。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，查尔斯·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
“所以我明白当我们谈论‘这辆车不适合这位车手’时，但[埃尔顿]塞纳并没有一个糟糕的公式。[迈克尔]舒马赫也没有一个糟糕的公式。汉密尔顿，他是不是有一个糟糕的公式，还是只是疲劳？这位车手已经存在很久了；关系会变得疲劳。也许他那时对这项运动的热爱并不够，但他以他反弹的方式让我印象深刻。
“今天对他来说比查尔斯要困难一些，但我并不完全同意这一代不适合这位车手。”
梅赛德斯车手基米·安东内利，他在F1的第二赛季，有机会在美国大奖赛上赢得他的第一个冠军。虽然他赢得了比赛，但他的竞争对手乔治·罗素和刘易斯·汉密尔顿也获得了足够的分数，使得比赛一直持续到墨西哥大奖赛。
detailEn: David Coulthard rejects F1 regulation excuses with Ayrton Senna and Michael Schumacher comparison
David Coulthard has dismissed claims that Formula 1's 2026 regulations are to blame for drivers' struggles
David Coulthard on the grid during the Sprint
Motorsport culture beyond the track. Driver lifestyle, fashion, travel, design and the stories that make racing more than a sport.

Former Formula 1 driver David Coulthard has dismissed the narrative that drivers can blame poor performance on the championship's new 2026 regulations, insisting the all-time greats successfully adapt to any machinery.

F1 introduced a major regulation change in 2026. While several drivers have struggled to extract consistent pace from the new generation of cars, Coulthard argued that a driver's baseline performance should remain unaffected by the rulebook.
Speaking on the Up To Speed podcast following the United States Grand Prix, the 13-time grand prix winner drew on his own career to reject the idea that specific cars do not suit certain drivers.

"I drove active cars, passive cars, 3.5-litre, 3-litre, 2.4-litre, groove tyres, slick tyres, tyre wars, and my performance throughout all of those was relatively the same, quite frankly, in that I lacked a 10th in qualifying and that makes it difficult for you to get track position against your team-mate," Coulthard explained.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

"So I understand when we talk about, 'This car doesn't suit this driver,' but [Ayrton] Senna didn't really have a bad formula. [Michael] Schumacher didn't have a bad formula. Hamilton, did he have a bad formula or was it just fatigue? The guy's been around forever; relationships get fatigued. Maybe his love for the sport at that time just wasn't quite there, but he's amazed me with the way he's bounced back.
"Today was a little bit more tricky for him than for Charles, but I'm not sure I really buy into this generation doesn't suit this driver."

Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who is in his second season in F1, had the chance to claim his first championship at the United States Grand Prix. While he won the race, his title rivals George Russell and Lewis Hamilton scored enough to keep the fight going to the Mexican Grand Prix.

items.titleZh: 拉塞尔美国站速度糟糕，与安东内利反差鲜明
items.summaryZh: 拉塞尔在美国大奖赛正赛仅列第八，落后夺冠的队友安东内利54秒，他将自己的速度形容为“糟糕透顶”。
items.originalTitle: The brutal Mercedes contrasts behind Russell's 'rubbish' pace
items.summaryEn: George Russell finished eighth at the United States Grand Prix, 54 seconds behind race winner and Mercedes team-mate Kimi Antonelli, describing his own pace as "rubbish".
detailZh: 困惑的乔治·拉塞尔对美国大奖赛上自己“糟糕”的速度找不到答案，这与志在夺冠的F1队友基米·安东内利形成了残酷反差。
拉塞尔最终第八完赛，落后分站冠军安东内利54秒；安东内利如今几乎已锁定在下周日墨西哥大奖赛加冕F1世界冠军。
安东内利本不太可能在奥斯汀就锁定冠军，但两位梅赛德斯车手之间的境遇差距如此之大，他差一点就提前做到了。
拉塞尔最终的差距和低迷名次，因五秒罚时的后果而被放大——这让他在比赛后半段被困在迈凯伦的奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里身后；但他对天空体育F1直言：“今天速度就是糟糕，这就是全部。
“那五秒大概让我丢了两三个位置。但在需要拿出速度的时候，速度不够好。”
拉塞尔尤其对糟糕的第一段 stint（ stint）感到警觉，这段表现甚至无法用陷入车流来合理解释，因为随着比赛推进，他落后伊萨克·哈贾尔的红牛赛车几秒钟。
这里本应有一些脏空气效应，但远不足以解释为什么拉塞尔平均每圈比安东内利慢零点八秒，并且越落越远，以至于早早采用两停策略的马克斯·维斯塔潘和夏尔·勒克莱尔都追上并重新超越了他，之后拉塞尔才终于进站。
拉塞尔称落后这么多很奇怪，随后不久他对包括 The Race 在内的媒体讲话时也没有答案，承认：“我需要给自己 24 小时来理清思路。”
第一段长距离 阶段是拉塞尔将整场比赛总结为“六圈好、五十圈糟”的重要原因。他第二次长距离使用硬胎的开局——在追上皮亚斯特里之前——是唯一相对亮点，但即便那时他也比安东内利每圈慢约零点一到零点二秒：更接近了，但仍然更慢，而且这是 stint 中可比较的部分，因为拉塞尔追皮亚斯特里时，安东内利也在追勒克莱尔。
“第一段 stint 节奏不好，但当我用硬胎出维修区后，大概有六圈我的圈速和基米一样，”拉塞尔说。“但后来我追上了奥斯卡，就是超不过去。”
皮亚斯特里的防守——以及/或者拉塞尔令人意外的难以发动进攻，仅在第37圈尝试一次便被挡回——确实毁了拉塞尔的比赛。他被困在皮亚斯特里的节奏里，迈凯伦让拉长的一停策略奏效，因此无法与安东内利的节奏直接比较。
不过拉塞尔的注意力在别处，因此强调：“我想弄明白为什么第一段 stint 节奏这么差。”但让困惑更深的是他补充道：“我需要和车队深入挖掘，因为当你落后这么多时，很难理解。”
目前所有的都只是理论。安东内利证明了升级后的梅赛德斯确实拥有出色的峰值表现，但拉塞尔可能正受困于人们谈论的那个狭窄的平衡窗口。
还有他们驾驶这些赛车和引擎的方式。拉塞尔和皮亚斯特里——领先车队中这一代赛车最挣扎的两位车手——本周末被队友碾压，这不可能只是巧合。
其中一部分原因一定在于他们在慢弯中操控赛车的舒适程度。在奥斯汀的排位赛中，拉塞尔在较快弯角能与安东内利匹敌，但在其他地方却持续落后。
安东内利显然更乐于应对车尾的滑动，并且在平衡推进程度而不让轮胎过度受力方面更为精准——但在奥斯汀，他总体上也更愿意牺牲一点入弯速度来最大化出弯表现。
如下方轨迹图所示，从12号弯到15号弯的损失被绘制出来，差值根据他们不同的入弯速度处理方式和出弯跑法而下降和上升，但最终安东内利在这一段结束时获得了决定性优势。
这也是安东内利相对于其他赛车特别强势的地方，而拉塞尔自从在这一段之前的11号弯出现一个小失误以来，就逐渐失去了对后轮温度的控制。
在排位赛中，拉塞尔在每个明显的慢速弯出弯处都比安东内利慢，而这些出弯处通常也通向主要的部署区域。
这里可能存在双重打击：安东内利在出弯和进入直道时携带更多速度，而且他在全油门方面的效率天生更高。而拉塞尔可能在不高效的油门区间花费更多时间。
梅赛德斯车队老板托托·沃尔夫推测，拉塞尔在梅赛德斯以领先姿态开启周末时表现最强，但当车队发现情况更艰难时，他受到的困扰更大——如果升级的特性会放大这种不适，这可能是第一个真实的例子。
“当我们将赛车调整到适合他的方式时，他绝对很快，”沃尔夫说。“但当它掉出那个工作窗口时，他就会挣扎。而且他比基米可能挣扎得更多。这是我们的责任。
“我们只需要和他一起弄清楚，为什么驾驶表现会有这么大的差异，因为乔治并不是比基米慢半秒、慢十分之三秒。绝对根本不是这种情况。
“那么他不喜欢的是什么？我们需要在改装赛车、以不同方式设置赛车让他跑快方面做些什么？”
在赛季已经深入到这个阶段还在问这些问题，考虑到拉塞尔近期的进步，这并不理想——他此前似乎在逐步缩小赛季中期对安东内利出现的最严重劣势。
但也值得强调，安东内利在奥斯汀表现极为出色，因此给拉塞尔形成了格外鲜明的反差。尽管外界对拉塞尔的状态百思不得其解，沃尔夫也承认，梅赛德斯本赛季同样没有预料到安东内利会有如此大的进步，而这正是他成长为一名高质量车手的最新例证。
安东内利在排位赛中表现出色，在赛车最强的环节充分压榨出圈速，也就是第一赛段的中高速连续弯，并且出色地控制后轮打滑，弥补了赛车整个周末在低速12、13和15号弯最薄弱的环节。
而在正赛中，得益于身后赛车互相缠斗、早早给他带来两秒的缓冲，他通过保持稳定优势，立刻化解了使用软胎的对手对他中性胎可能构成的任何威胁。
随后他毫无波澜地完成了一次进站策略，尽管对硬胎并不熟悉，而且策略是在第一段 stint 后于比赛中期才锁定的。甚至他在赛道限制上频繁试探的倾向，在关键时刻也完全得到了控制。
“在基米这边，主要的头条是，对我来说，这是他迄今为止奉献的最棒的一场比赛，”沃尔夫说道。“这是一场尚未成为冠军的冠军所展现的比赛，但非常出色。”
在一个标准极高的赛季中，这是一个大胆的论断——其中包括在摩纳哥的惊艳表现，以及最著名的，安东内利在蒙扎从第19位发车夺冠。或许安东内利最令人印象深刻的是他完成这一切的轻松自如。
没有锁定冠军的压力，因为一段时间以来这实际上已是板上钉钉的事，但即便经历了本赛季最大的失误——在阿塞拜疆排位赛中撞车——以及梅赛德斯随后在赛车升级上的波动，他依然毫不松懈。
这是两位车手之间形成鲜明对比的又一个例子。拉塞尔在顺境中拼得更凶，在逆境中则更容易、也更戏剧性地陷入低谷。对安东内利来说，这一切都如此自然，显得毫不费力，让他能够反复攀上新的高度——因此他认为，就自己和车队所做的工作而言，这一站的表现超过了蒙扎。
“蒙扎，我们显然拥有最快的赛车，”安东内利说。“我们就是超级快，所以从后面追上来当然非常特别，但那也是一条相对容易超车的赛道，而且我们那么快。
“毫无疑问，蒙扎是非常特别的一站，也是我会永远记住的一站。但这一站，就执行层面而言，可能更好，因为我们逐步积累、在整个周末逐步提升表现的方式非常出色。”
detailEn: A confused George Russell lacked answers for his “rubbish” pace at the United States Grand Prix, which contrasted brutally with his championship-bound Formula 1 team-mate Kimi Antonelli.
Russell finished eighth and 54 seconds behind race winner Antonelli, who is now all but guaranteed to become F1 world champion in next Sunday’s Mexican Grand Prix.
It was unlikely that Antonelli would seal the deal in Austin but such was the difference in fortunes between the Mercedes drivers he very nearly pulled it off.

Russell’s final margin and his lowly position was exaggerated by the consequences of a five-second penalty that meant he got stuck behind McLaren’s Oscar Piastri in the second half of the race, but as he bluntly told Sky Sports F1: “The pace was just rubbish today, that’s the long and short of it.
“The five seconds probably cost me two or three positions. But the pace was not good enough when it needed to be.”

Russell was particularly alarmed by a poor opening stint that cannot even be explained satisfactorily by being in traffic, because he slipped back a few seconds behind Isack Hadjar’s Red Bull as it progressed.

There would have been some dirty air effect here, but not nearly enough to explain why Russell was eight tenths a lap slower than Antonelli on average and drifted so far away that early two-stoppers Max Verstappen and Charles Leclerc had caught and re-passed him before Russell finally came in.
Russell called it strange to be so far off, and when he spoke to media including The Race shortly afterwards he had no answers, admitting: “I need to give myself 24 hours to think clearly”.

That first stint is a large part of why Russell summed his race up as “six good laps, 50 bad laps”. The start of his second long stint on hards - before catching Piastri - the only relative bright spot, but even then he seemed around a tenth or two slower than Antonelli: closer, but still slower, and this is a comparable part of the stint because while Russell was catching Piastri, Antonelli was catching Leclerc.

“The pace wasn't good on the first stint, but when I came out of pits on the hard, I probably did six laps where I was lapping the same pace as Kimi,” Russell said. “But then I caught Oscar and I just couldn't overtake.”

Piastri’s defence - and/or Russell’s surprising difficulty in making a move, with only a single attempt on lap 37 rebuffed - did indeed kill Russell’s race. He was stuck at Piastri’s pace as McLaren made a stretched one-stop work, and so a direct comparison with Antonelli’s pace was not possible.

Russell’s focus was elsewhere, though, hence stressing: “I want to understand why the pace was so bad on the first stint”. But to compound the confusion he added: “I need to dig deep with my team because it's difficult to understand when you're so far off.”
All there are, for now, are theories. Antonelli proved that the upgraded Mercedes does have a wonderful peak, but Russell may be suffering from the narrow balance window that has been talked about.

There’s also the way they simply drive these cars and engines. It cannot be a coincidence that Russell and Piastri, the two chief strugglers of this generation of car among the leading teams, received a pasting from their team-mates this weekend.

Some of that must be in how comfortable they are manipulating the car in slow corners. Russell was there with Antonelli in the faster turns in qualifying at Austin, but consistently losing out elsewhere.

Antonelli definitely seems happier living with the rear moving around and is more precise in balancing how much to push that without over-stressing the tyres – but in Austin he was also, generally, willing to sacrifice a little bit of corner entry speed to maximise his exit.

As the below trace shows, charting the loss from Turn 12 to 15, the delta falls and rises based on their different entry speed approaches and runs off the corner, but it culminates in Antonelli eventually having a decisive advantage by the end of the sequence.

This is where Antonelli was particularly strong versus other cars too, whereas Russell has gradually lost control of rear tyre temperature ever since a small error way back before this sequence at Turn 11.
Russell was slower than Antonelli on every prominent slower corner exit in qualifying, and these usually lead into the main deployment zones too.

There could be a double whammy here, with Antonelli carrying more speed off the corner and onto the straight, but also being inherently more efficient in how he is often sharper onto full throttle. Whereas Russell potentially spends more time in an inefficient throttle range.

Mercedes team boss Toto Wolff theorised that Russell has been strongest when Mercedes has started weekends on the front foot but suffered more when it has found things tougher - if the upgrade’s characteristics can exaggerate that discomfort, this could have been the first real example of it.

“When we land the car in the way that suits him, he's absolutely fast,” said Wolff. “But when it drops out of that operating window, he struggles. And he struggles more than maybe Kimi. And that is on us.

“ We just have to work it out with him how there can be such a difference in driving in performance because George is not half a second slower, three tenths slower than Kimi. It's just absolutely not the case.
“So what is it that he doesn't like? What is it that we need to do in terms of modifying the car, setting it up in a different way for him to go fast?”

That these questions are still being asked deep into the season is not great given the recent progress Russell seemed to have made, chipping away at the worst of his deficit to Antonelli that emerged through the middle of the season.

But it’s also worth stressing that Antonelli was magnificent at Austin, and therefore presented Russell with an especially harsh contrast. For all of the head-scratching over Russell’s form, Wolff has admitted that Mercedes didn’t see such a big step from Antonelli this season coming either, with this being the latest example of what a high-quality driver he has evolved into.

Antonelli excelled in qualifying to wring the neck out of the car in its strongest parts around the lap, namely the medium and high speed Esses in the opening sector, and control the rear tyre slip excellently to mitigate where it had been weakest all weekend in the slow-speed Turns 12, 13 and 15.

And in the race, aided by cars squabbling behind and giving him a two-second buffer early on, he immediately neutralised any threat he might have faced from those on softs to his mediums by maintaining a steady advantage.

Then he executed a one-stop without any hint of fuss, despite unfamiliarity with the hard tyre and the strategy being locked in mid-race after the first stint. Even his tendency to flirt extensively with track limits seemed totally under control when it counted.
“On Kimi's side, the main headline is that, for me, the best race that he's delivered so far,” Wolff said. “The race of a champion who isn't the champion yet, but exceptional.”

That is a big claim in a season of extremely high standards that includes a tremendous showing in Monaco and, most famously, Antonelli’s win from 19th on the grid at Monza. Perhaps what was most impressive about Antonelli was the ease with which he produced this.

There is no pressure to secure the title, because it has been effectively a foregone conclusion for a while, but he has been relentless even through his biggest mistake of the season - crashing in qualifying in Azerbaijan - and Mercedes’ subsequent wobble with its car upgrade.

That is another example of the contrast between the two drivers. Russell’s fighting harder for the good moments and falls into the bad ones more easily and dramatically. For Antonelli, this is all so natural, and comes across as effortless, allowing him to repeatedly scale new heights - hence his agreement this topped Monza in terms of the job he and the team did.

“Monza, we clearly had the fastest car,” said Antonelli. “We were just super quick, so of course it was incredibly special coming from the back, but it was also a track where it was relatively easy to overtake, and we were so quick.

“Definitely, Monza was a super special one, and one that I will remember forever. But, this one probably, in terms of execution, was better, because the way we built up and the way we built the performance throughout the weekend was very good.”
